chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his men, raising it (marfu'), said:

Tamim al-Dari, Ibn Baydi, and Ibn Abi Mariya went out on a journey. Tamim al-Dari was a Muslim, and Ibn Baydi and Ibn Abi Mariya were two Christians. With Tamim al-Dari was a bag containing goods, vessels engraved with gold, and a necklace, which he had brought out to one of the Arab markets for sale. Tamim al-Dari fell severely ill, and when death approached him, he handed over what was with him to Ibn Baydi and Ibn Abi Mariya, and instructed them both to deliver it to his heirs. So they both proceeded to Medina, having taken from the baggage the vessels and the necklace, and delivered the rest to his heirs.

So the people noticed the absence of the vessels and the necklace, and the family of Tamim said to them: 'Was our companion ill for a long time and spent much on expenses?' They said: 'No, he was only sick for a few days.' They said: 'Was anything stolen from him on this journey?' They said: 'No.' They said: 'Did he trade and incur a loss?' They said: 'No.' They said: 'We are missing the finest things that were with him — vessels engraved with gold adorned with gems, and a necklace.' They said: 'Whatever was handed to us, we have delivered to you.' So they were brought before the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and the Messenger of God imposed an oath upon both of them. They swore, and he released them. Then those vessels and the necklace were found to be in their possession. So the guardians of Tamim came to the Messenger of God and said: 'O Messenger of God! What we claimed against Ibn Baydi and Ibn Abi Mariya has been proven.' So the Messenger of God awaited the ruling from God, Mighty and Majestic, in that matter.

Then God, Blessed and Exalted, revealed: 'O you who believe! Take as witnesses between you two just persons from among you, or two others from outside you, when death approaches one of you at the time of making a will, if you are traveling in the land.' So God, Mighty and Majestic, permitted the testimony of the People of the Book for the bequest only, when one is traveling and cannot find Muslims. 'When the calamity of death befalls you, detain the two witnesses after prayer; then if you doubt them, they shall both swear by God: "We will not sell it for any price, even if a relative, and we will not conceal the testimony of God — for then we would certainly be among the sinners."' This is the first testimony which the Messenger of God established.

'Then if it becomes known that both have been guilty of sin' — meaning they swore falsely — 'then two others shall stand in their place from among those who have the rightful claim, the two who are nearest' — meaning from the guardians of the claimant, those against whom the two originally stood — 'and they shall swear by God: "Certainly our testimony is truer than the testimony of those two, and we have not exceeded the limit — for then we would certainly be among the wrongdoers."' So the Messenger of God ordered the guardians of Tamim al-Dari to swear by God as He had commanded them. So they swore.

And the Messenger of God seized the necklace and the vessels from Ibn Baydi and Ibn Abi Mariya and returned them to the guardians of Tamim al-Dari. 'That is more proper so that they will give testimony in its true form, or fear that oaths will be turned back after their oaths.'

key_terms.أَهْل الْكِتَاب: People of the Book — Jews and Christians; their testimony is permitted under exceptional circumstances
key_terms.أَوْلِيَاء: Guardians/heirs — the rightful claimants to the deceased's estate
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّة: Bequest, last will — the instruction given before death regarding one's estate
key_terms.الْيَمِين: Oath — the sworn testimony required to validate the witnesses' claims
key_terms.شَهَادَة: Testimony, witnessing — here referring to the legal testimony required for bequests

ai.seo_question: What is the occasion of revelation for Quran 5:106-108 about testimony and bequests?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the occasion of revelation for Quran 5:106–108, the verses on testimony during travel and bequests. During the time of the Prophet Muhammad, Tameem al-Dari, a Companion, fell ill on a journey and entrusted his possessions to two Christian companions who later embezzled part of his estate. When brought before the Prophet, they initially swore an oath of innocence, but the stolen goods were later found with them. The Prophet awaited divine guidance, and these three Quranic verses were revealed, establishing the rules for testimony by non-Muslims in cases where a Muslim cannot find Muslim witnesses during travel.
